title: Three Evenings and One Short Candle
subtitle: 节日庆典 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）
meta: 主题语境：节日庆典（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·节日与庆典）　|　核心词汇：lantern　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lantern 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the maker ① hung the lantern that no neighbour in the street would have recorded, and he said the hanging was the whole of the evening. The ② lantern, meaning the light itself and not the candle, ran three evenings and stayed unrecorded in the book; a lantern, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ lantern in that street had the same short candle beside it, and the ④ lantern at the far gate, meaning the paper they kept for the children to paste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A lantern, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the maker said the recording is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the lantern was the whole of the matter, meaning the wish and not the light. The ⑥ lantern, meaning the wish and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; lantern, he said, is either something you hang or the only word that means both a light and a wish. He said the wish is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ lantern had become a line in a song, and the song had become an argument about the short candle. The ⑧ lantern of the whole thing, the maker wrote in February, was one street and three evenings of recording; lantern, he said, is either the paper at the far gate or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ lantern I remember is the light recorded in the song, which closed in 1960 and is still recorded as the quietest in the street. A ⑩ lantern, my mother said in 1962, is the only light that improves by being recorded; every lantern, she said, is a wish that has agreed to look like a light. She said the wish was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 灯笼；灯（指街巷里每一盏旁边的那一盏）
B. n. 灯笼；灯（指那盏灯笼本身，与蜡烛相对）
C. 固定搭配：hang the lantern 挂起这盏灯笼
D. n. 灯笼；灯（指留给孩子们糊上的那张纸那一盏）
E. n. 灯会之事（抽象总称，指一处街巷的灯笼之事）
F. n. 灯笼；灯（指灯歌里写到、被记载的的那一盏）
G. n. 心愿、祈愿（指一件事里人人都挂却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 祈愿（抽象总称，指人人都挂却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: hung the lantern that no neighbour in the street would have recorded
The lantern, meaning the light itself and not the candle
the lantern at the far gate
the lantern was the whole of the matter
the lantern had become a line in a song
The lantern of the whole thing
A lantern, my mother said in 1962

answers.why: hang the lantern 意为“挂起这盏灯笼”，1953 年那位扎灯匠把街巷里没有一位街坊肯记载的一盏灯笼做了一遍。
lantern 意为“灯笼；灯”，指那盏灯笼本身而不是蜡烛，它经过了三个傍晚而在簿子上没有被记载。
lantern 意为“灯笼；灯”，指街巷里每一盏旁边的那一盏，每一盏旁边都有同一支小小的蜡烛。
lantern 意为“灯笼；灯”，指最远那座门楼留给孩子们糊上的那张纸那一盏，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
lantern 意为“心愿、祈愿”，指一件事里人人都挂却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份心愿就是那件事的全部。
lantern 意为“祈愿”，指人人都挂却无人提起的那样东西而不是那盏灯笼，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
lantern 意为“灯笼；灯”，指灯歌里写到、被记载的的那一盏，到 1958 年这一盏成了灯歌里的一行。
lantern 意为“灯会之事”，扎灯匠二月写道，整件事的灯笼之事是一处街巷和三个傍晚的记载。
lantern 意为“灯笼；灯”，我记得的是灯歌里记载过的那一盏，1960 年挂好了，至今仍被说成街巷里最安静的一盏。
lantern 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，灯笼是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的灯笼。
